name: Baofeng BF-1909
notes: BENCH CONFIRMED 2026-10-09 against a physical unit (instance eam_1909_01) on m2uehlair over a CH340 cable at /dev/cu.usbserial-110. A read-only CHIRP sync_in returned a full 1008-byte image, exactly the driver's _memsize of 0x03F0, and the image decoded to 16 channel slots with no name field and no banks -- so limits.max_channels 16, the omitted max_channel_name_chars, and max_zones 1 are all confirmed against hardware, not just inferred from the driver. The WRITE path is confirmed too: a codeplugger-generated 16-channel plan was written with sync_out and the subsequent re-read came back byte-identical to the staged image (0 bytes differing, 160 differing from the factory content), then the factory image was written back and re-read to md5 c2d2531583b1fbc33774cefcd2a73f79, matching as-found exactly. Note the test plan was deliberately chosen to differ from the factory content -- a round-trip identity write cannot distinguish a successful write from a silent no-op. CHIRP registers this as driver key Baofeng_BF-1909, Vendor Model string "Baofeng BF-1909", so id/name/chirp.model all agree for once -- unlike the BF-888S, where the case and the driver disagree. The driver is BF1909Radio in chirp/drivers/h777.py, a subclass of BF1901Radio and therefore of H777Radio: the BF-1909 is an H-777 family radio and speaks the same clone protocol as the BF-888S, at 9600 baud with PROGRAM_CMD b'PWPG970' inherited from BF-1901. Driver figures were read off chirp-src at commit 098f57b (2026-09-12). limits.max_channels 16 is the driver's memory_bounds (1, 16) and the radio's 16-position channel knob. max_channel_name_chars is omitted because there is no channel-name field: the driver sets rf.has_name = False, the radio has no display, and every slot in the unit we read came back with an empty name. A channel is identified only by knob position, so channel names in a profile are operator documentation, not data the radio stores. (valid_name_length reports 6, but that is the inherited H-777 default and is dead with has_name False -- do not model it.) max_zones 1 is the usual shim for a radio with no zone concept, rf.has_bank = False, confirmed on the read image. modes is ["FM"]: valid_modes are NFM/FM with no AM. bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 is the narrow bit in the channel record, matching CHIRP's NFM/FM. Every channel in the as-shipped image was NFM. IDENTITY GATE -- the unit we read answers the programming handshake with b'P320h\xF4AM'. Checked against every H-777 family driver CHIRP registers, that ident matches Baofeng_BF-1909 and nothing else: BF-1901, BF-1904, BF-888, BF-M4, MP31, Maverick RA-100/RA-425, MaxTalker MT-8S, Radioddity GA-2S and Retevis H777/H777 Plus all key on b'P3107', which is not a substring of b'P320h\xF4AM'. So on this unit the model is unambiguous. Be aware the driver's IDENT list is [b'P320h', b'P3107\xF4AM'] and that SECOND entry does contain the b'P3107' prefix the rest of the family matches on -- a BF-1909 that identifies with that string would be ambiguous against a BF-888S, and would need _memsize 0x03F0 and _ranges [(0x0000,0x0110),(0x0250,0x0260),(0x02B0,0x02C0),(0x03C0,0x03E0)] to separate it from the 888S's 0x03E0. Separately, match_model() is hardcoded to return False with the comment "This model is only ever matched via metadata", so CHIRP will never auto-detect a BF-1909 from a raw .img; the model must be selected explicitly. BAND -- STILL THE WEAKEST CLAIM IN THIS FILE, AND BENCH WORK DID NOT SETTLE IT. The single 400-470 MHz transmit span follows the BF-888S/W31E treatment, with nothing receive-only. It is deliberately tighter than the driver's VALID_BANDS of 400-520 MHz, which BF1909Radio inherits unchanged from BF1901Radio and which is a catch-all covering the wider BF-19xx family, not a fact about this radio. 400-470 MHz is the transmit range Baofeng's retail listings publish for this model and several independent sellers agree on it. That is still the only evidence behind the number: no FCC ID and no case marking have been read off the unit, and reading a codeplug tells you what someone programmed, not what the PA and the approval allow. If an FCC ID is read and its grant covers a narrower span, tighten this band to match -- an approval record may only narrow the transmit range here, never widen it. One real data point in favour of a span wider than 446: the unit accepted and read back a full set of 462 MHz channels, so whatever market it shipped for, its firmware is NOT locked to the PMR446 block. That bounds the firmware, not the PA and not the grant. The unit we read shipped on the EUROPEAN PMR446 grid, not a US plan: all 16 slots were factory-filled with 446.00625 through 446.19375 MHz on 12.5 kHz spacing, NFM, high power, with DTCS 023 on channels 1-4 and TSQL 141.3 on channel 5. That is the 16-channel PMR446 allocation exactly, which is a strong hint this is an EU-market unit and a reason to actually read its label before trusting a US-sourced 400-470 MHz figure. Note the trap for US operators: 446 MHz is licence-free PMR446 in Europe but sits inside the US 70 cm amateur band, so those factory channels are NOT license-free here and must not be keyed up without an amateur licence. Which slice of 400-470 MHz an operator may use is licence and jurisdiction policy and belongs in a profile; capabilities states what the hardware transmits on. Driver power levels are 1 W low / 10 W high, but the 1 W figure is NOT authoritative: upstream carries a literal "# TODO: Is it 1 watt?" comment directly above POWER_LEVELS, so the low setting is an upstream guess. Neither level has been measured here. HEADLESS READ GOTCHA: h777.do_download() calls radio.pipe.log(...), which the CHIRP GUI satisfies with chirp.wxui.serialtrace.SerialTrace, a serial.Serial subclass. Hand a driver a bare pyserial Serial and the read dies partway through the block loop with AttributeError: 'Serial' object has no attribute 'log'. For headless reads, pass a serial.Serial subclass with a no-op log() method rather than importing the wx-dependent wrapper.
